draft.title: First-person narration
card: A first-person narrator is a character who tells the story using I and me. Example: "I shut the gate and felt my stomach tighten."
The reader gets close to the narrator's thoughts and feelings, so the story can feel personal and honest.
The reader sees only what the narrator knows, sees and believes. The narrator cannot know what other characters think unless they are told.
Because the narrator has opinions, the reader may sense that the account is one-sided or mistaken. The narrator's view is not always the whole truth.
draft.remember: First person means I: close to one mind, but limited to what that person knows and believes.

a.q: Which sentence is written from a first-person narrator's point of view?
opts: I hid the letter, hoping nobody had noticed
She hid the letter, hoping nobody had noticed
You hide the letter, hoping nobody has noticed
Tariq hid the letter while the whole class watched
a.why: The word I shows that the narrator is a character telling their own story. The she and Tariq options use third person, and you speaks to the reader.
a.clue: Look for the pronoun the narrator uses for themselves.

b.q: Priya narrates a story as I. Her friend Jo goes quiet at lunch, and Priya says Jo must be angry with her. Why might a reader doubt this?
opts: Priya can only guess at Jo's feelings from her own view
Priya is telling the story in the past tense
Jo is a minor character, so she has no feelings
First-person narrators always lie to the reader
b.why: A first-person narrator knows only what she sees and believes, so her guess about Jo may be wrong. It is not true that such narrators always lie: they are limited, not necessarily dishonest.
b.clue: Can Priya see inside Jo's head?

a.best: I hid the letter, hoping nobody had noticed

b.best: Priya can only guess at Jo's feelings from her own view
